$comment: The ONE source of every permission pack (zheref/hatsu#85). These are the commands Hatsu's skills actually run, scoped to the repository the session stands in, its linked worktrees, and the repositories nen/repos.json declares as associated (consumers, maintained_tools). Anything outside that scope -- another repository, a system setting, a credential store, an elevation -- is deliberately absent and keeps prompting. scripts/permissions_pack.sh renders this file into each surface's own permission and hook files; the maintainer's rulings of 2026-09-19: a session is never asked about an action scoped to the current project or its associated repositories. The deny rows are a second line: hooks/guard-base-branch.sh is the guard that parses a push and refuses the base branch and force forms whatever the spelling.

scope.repository: the checkout the session stands in
scope.worktrees: every linked worktree of that checkout (git rev-parse --git-common-dir)
scope.associated: repositories nen/repos.json lists under consumers, maintained_tools or pending_onboarding
scope.enforced_by: Codex only, through sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots. Claude Code and Cursor allowlists are exe-and-argument PATTERNS with no root syntax: their scope is that the rendered file lives in this checkout's own .claude/ or .cursor/ directory and applies to sessions opened there, and nothing in the file refuses an allowed command pointed at another checkout. The deny rows and hooks/guard-base-branch.sh are the second line on every surface.

$comment_removed_gh_auth_token: REMOVED (Feitan F1, 2026-09-20): the shared allow list used to carry {exe: gh, args: 'auth token'}. Every verb that needs GH_TOKEN reads it out of gh's OWN credential store at call time (gh api/pr/issue/run/label all resolve auth internally) -- nothing in this codebase pipes 'gh auth token' output anywhere it needs to be. Allowing the bare command meant a session could run it and have the live OAuth token printed straight into the transcript, which is a credential leak an allowlist exists to prevent, not to grant.

surfaces.$comment: Per-surface rows transcribed verbatim after the shared allow list, for that surface only (nen surface mirror generate --permissions, v0.13.0). Cursor has no implicit file access in cli.json, so its pack declares tree-wide read and write here rather than the generator adding them unasked (Feitan, 2026-09-20).

codex.$comment: Codex's verbs reach the network on purpose: en/mukai's PR verbs fetch from github.com, hanten's reviewer raise pushes a worktree branch, and getsuga/backlog verbs call `gh`. nen's surface-mirror generator emits the Codex config.toml `network_access` line from this declaration alone (v0.13.0) — remove it here and the generated surface goes network-closed under those verbs.
